sentences.text: Brief case of prosecution is that deceased Poonam was married to the accused on 11.05.2011 at native place of both the parties at Basti, U.P. After that on 08.05.2013 gauna ceremony was solemnized and the deceased went to her in-laws home.
However, after about 12 days she returned to Delhi because deceased had to continue her studies.

The accused, who was living at his native State vs Harikesh on 3 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126050757/
1 place in Basti, never attempted take deceased back and the father of the accused used to make excuse that he is still young and is not earning.

Deceased had again visited her matrimonial home on 03.02.2016 as the father of accused has called the parents of deceased and she remained there till 30.05.2016 only and again returned back because she had to continue her fashion designing course.

Thereafter, the deceased continue to remain with her parents till she committed suicide by living suicide note Ex.P-2.
2.

On 30.07.2016 while the deceased was at her parents home with younger sister, when her parents were not there, deceased shut herself in the room and committed suicide by hanging, leaving the suicide note which is reproduced herein below:
"Mein apni life se hi dukhi ho gyi hun.
Mein jo karne ja rahi hu usme mere mummy papa ka of na hi kisi bhi friends ka kasur hai.
Meri life bahut hi khrab ho chuki hain.
Mein apni shadi se bahut dukhi hu.
Iski wajah se maine SC No. 53630/2016 State Vs. Harikesh Page no. 2 of 17 yeh kadam uthaya hain.
Mujhe apni sadhi se bahut umeed thi par aisa kuch nhi hua.
Mujhe bahut problem hain.
Main ab jeena nahi chahti hun.

In sab mein meri mummy papa ki koi galti nahi hain.
Problem bas itni thi ki mujhe samaj nahi ske.
I am sorry mummy papa agar appko dukhi kiya to.
Bas mujhe itna hi likhna tha mein nahi chahti ki mere jaane ke baad meri mummy papa or mere sabhi friends ko koi problem kisi baat ki."
3. The police was informed about the incident vide DD no. 29 PP when the father of deceased took the deceased to hospital and examined her vide MLC Ex.Pw7/A.
On this DD entry, the IO reached at hospital where the hand written suicide note of deceased was handed over by the father to the IO.
Therefore, the SDM was informed and the spot was inspected.

It was also mentioned by the parents of deceased that on 10.07.2016 when they had went to the marriage of their nephew at Basti, the accused had quarreled with deceased and after returning to Delhi the deceased told them that the accused SC No. 53630/2016 State Vs. 8. After completion of PE, accused was examined under Section 313 Cr.P.C./351 BNSS in which accused claimed innocence and stated that he never demanded any money or any material from deceased.

10. Prosecution would submits that parents of deceased have specifically deposed that accused used to demand money from deceased and deceased was not treated with respect and was regularly abused.
Therefore, as the deceased committed suicide within 07 years of marriage, the presumption under Section 113 B Evidence Act comes into play, which the defence has failed to rebut.

Therefore,
the prosecution has proved all the charges.
SC No. 53630/2016 State Vs. Harikesh Page no. 8 of 17 11.
Per contra defence would submit that the entire case of prosecution is based on falsehood.
Defence would point to the fact that there is no previous complaint of any demand or any misbehavior with the deceased committed by accused.

Defence would also submit that in the marriage of five years, for initial two years the deceased was not sent to her matrimonial home because she was studying of which there was no objection form the side of accused and even after goana deceased remained with the accused and his family members for only few days.

It is submitted that for entire period of this marriage deceased had lived with her parents and perhaps they were forcing the deceased to join the company of accused which led the deceased to commit suicide and that is why deceased specifically mentioned in her suicide note that her parents failed to understand her.
Ld. Defence counsel would further refer to the suicide note and submit that had deceased had any problem with the accused she would have spelt that in clear terms.
The deceased was rather unhappy with her marriage as she had some different dreams.

Ld. Defence counsel further point out that except parents of deceased, there is no other witness to corroborate their version that the deceased was subjected to cruelty or harassment on account of dowry demand,
rather they have admitted that it was the accused who used to contribute in the education of deceased as accused used to send money in the account of the brother of deceased.
12. The suicide note Ex.P-1/P-2 do not shed any light about any any cruel treatment subjected by the deceased at the hands of SC No. 53630/2016 State Vs. Harikesh Page no. 9 of 17 accused or in-laws.

sentences.text: It only shows that deceased was not happy with the marriage as she had some different dreams.
It is a admitted fact that from the date of marriage on 11.05.2011 to the date of her death the deceased had lived with the accused at her matrimonial home only on two occasions.
On first occasion she went there on 08.05.2013 and returned after few days and on second occasion deceased went to her in-laws house on 03.02.216 and returned on 30.03.2016.
On both occasions she returned as she had to continue with her education.
On first occasion it was BA Examination time and on 2 nd occasion she was continuing with fashion designing course.
After her return on 30.05.2016, deceased committed suicide on 30.07.2016.
From 11.05.2011 or form May 2013 when she returned for the first time, till 30.07.2016 no compliant was ever made by Pw-10 or Pw-11 or by deceased about any misbehavior committed on deceased.
The allegation of dowry demand as well as harassment have surfaced only after death of deceased.

However, the fact that accused used to contribute for the education of the deceased, which has come only when the defence put those payments in cross examination, belies the parents of deceased that the accused used to demand money from her.

13. In the entire testimony, the only allegation of demand by accused is with respect to a demand of Rs. 5 lacs from the deceased which under the given facts that accused was contributing for her education appears to be an after thought.

However, even if it is assumed that the accused had State vs Harikesh on 3 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126050757/
5 demanded Rs. 5 lacs it was specifically for getting a job for the accused as SC No. 53630/2016 State Vs. Harikesh Page no. 10 of 17 he had to pay that money for securing his permanent job.

entities.text: State vs Harikesh on 3 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon

sentences.text: This demand was not in nature of dowry.

14. In Appasaheb And Anr vs State Of Maharashtra, 1 (2007) SLT 188 it was held by Hon'ble Supreme Court that:
9. Two essential ingredient of Section 304-B IPC, apart from others, are (i) death of women is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances, and (ii) women is subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for "dowry".

entities.text: Appasaheb And Anr vs State Of Maharashtra, 1 (2007) SLT 188
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The explanation appended to sub-section (1) of Section 304-B IPC says that "dowry" shall have the same meaning as in Section 2 of Dowry Prohibition Act,
1961.

Section 2 of Dowry Prohibition Act reads as under :-
"2. Definition of "dowry" - In this Act "dowry"

means any property or valuable security given or agreed to be given either directly or indirectly- (a) by one party to a marriage to the other party to the marriage; or (b) by the parent of either party to a marriage or by any other person, to either party to the marriage or to any other person, at or before or any time after the marriage in connection with the marriage of the said parties, but does not include dowry or mahr in the case of persons to whom the Muslim Personal Law (shariat) applies.

In view of the aforesaid definition of the word "dowry" any property or valuable security should be given or agreed to be given either directly or indirectly at or before or any time after the marriage and in connection with the marriage of the said parties.

Therefore, the giving or taking of SC No.
53630/2016 State Vs. Harikesh Page no. 11 of 17 property or valuable security must have some connection with the marriage of the parties and a correlation between the giving or taking of property or valuable security with the marriage of the parties is essential.
Being a penal provision it has to be strictly construed.
Dowry is a fairly well known social custom or practice in India.

It is well settled principle of interpretation of Statute that if the Act is passed with reference to a particular trade, business or transaction and words are used which everybody conversant with that trade,
business or transaction knows or understands to have a particular meaning in it, then the words are to be construed as having that particular meaning.

(See Union of India Vs. Garware Nylons Ltd.),
AIR (1996) SC 3509 and Chemicals and Fibers of India v. Union of India, AIR (1997) SC 558).

entities.text:
Union of India Vs. Garware Nylons Ltd.),
AIR (1996) SC 3509
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Chemicals and Fibers of India v. Union of India, AIR (1997) SC 558
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A demand for money on account of some financial stringency or for meeting some urgent domestic expenses of for purchasing manure cannot be termed as a demand for dowry as the said word is normally understood.

The evidence adduced by the prosecution does not, therefore, show that any State vs Harikesh on 3 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126050757/
6 demand for "dowry" as defined in Section 2 of the Dowry Prohibition Act was made by the appellants as what was allegedly asked for was some money for meeting domestic expenses and for purchasing manure.
Since an essential ingredient of Section 304-B IPC viz. demand for dowry is not established, the conviction of the appellants cannot be sustained.

15. As the only witnesses are the parents of deceased and it has come on record that the accused was aiding them in studies of deceased and there is no previous complaint to any person even any relative, it appears that these allegations of demanding Rs. 5 lacs are an afterthought.

If the suicide note is read carefully, SC No. 53630/2016 State Vs. Harikesh Page no. 12 of 17 the deceased appears to be exonerating her parents from putting her in that situation as they failed to understand her.
There is not a signal allegation, in the suicide note suggestive of any cruelty or harassment at the hands of accused.
There could not have been any because she lived at the house of the accused only for few days.
It appears that she committed suicide as she did not want to leave Delhi and she felt her dreams being shattered because of her marriage.
16. Thus, the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
The accused Harikesh is acquitted of the allegations levelled against him.

Since an essential ingredient of Section 304-B IPC viz. demand for dowry is not established, the conviction of the appellants cannot be sustained.
There is not a signal allegation, in the suicide note suggestive of any cruelty or harassment at the hands of accused.
There could not have been any because she lived at the house of the accused only for few days.
It appears that she committed suicide as she did not want to leave Delhi and she felt her dreams being shattered because of her marriage.
